newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies rally late to close up sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies rally late to close up sharply.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rallied in the last few minutes of trade to post a near limit gain before closing sharply higher. Hog futures followed on short covering to end mixed, traders said.

Pork bellies closed 2.625 to 0.075 cents per lb higher with February up 2.575 at 81.100 cents. Hogs finished 0.525 cent higher to 0.150 lower with February up most at 76.950 cents. July posted a new contract high of 78.350 cents.
Further commercial and technical demand pushed belly futures up into buy stops and prices shot up in the last five minutes of trade, they said.

Firm cash belly prices, as slaughter rates ran under expectations, added to the strong technical trend following Thursday's limit advance. Cargill Investor Services was a notable buyer before the run up, they said.
USDA reported cash belly prices were up two to three cents at midday and reported after the close that estimated hog slaughter for the week ran 17.3 percent under a year ago.
The light pace of slaughter comes while frozen storage stocks are low. There are not many deliverable bellies in storage with February approaching, traders added.

Stronger cash hog markets Friday and calls for steady to higher cash hog markets Monday kept hog futures supported despite profit taking. Nearby futures moved up to best levels late when the sharp runup in pork bellies prompted late short covering, traders said.

Expectations the hogs backed up from the last bout of wintry weather had weighed on prices into midweek, but the market turned firm when marketings dwindled. Cold weather again early next week may keep hog marketings lighter than expected, although those hogs will come to market sooner or larter, they added.

Rand Financials in LFG bought late. In that hog options LIT division of First Options bought February 77 calls and Cargill Investor Services sold February 78 calls early. Volatility was down sharply on time decay, pit sources said.
